wa_blues_cliff_the.blurb: A compact cliff in the middle tier of the Index Town Walls, in the Skykomish Valley east of Seattle. It holds about two dozen routes, most of them bolted, with a smaller number of trad lines, spread over slabs, corners and a few roofs. The grade range leans hard: the bulk of the climbing sits in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with only a couple of easier lines and a pair of routes at the 5.13 and 5.14 level. That makes it a place for strong sport climbers rather than beginners. The walk in is a steep switchback trail with several left-hand forks, and the middle walls generally see fewer people than the big faces lower down.

wa_tomato_wall.blurb: A short band of reddish basalt columns at the far western end of the Sunshine Wall at Frenchman Coulee, near Vantage in central Washington. About two dozen routes here are mostly trad crack climbs, with a handful of bolted lines, and the grades cluster between 5.8 and 5.10 with just one climb harder than that. It suits climbers stepping up from easy cracks and anyone wanting a quieter alternative to the busier central walls. The columns are shorter than elsewhere on the Sunshine Wall, and the end of the cliff has varied exposure, which can give some relief from wind or heat. Reach it by dropping down the third gully or walking the base trail west.

wa_toxic_tang_area.blurb: A cool, shady wall on the west side of the Inner Walls canyon at Index, in Washington's Skykomish Valley. The rock is granodiorite and is sharper-edged than the more knobby stone lower on the hillside. Around twenty routes mix trad and sport, from an easy 5.7 up through the 5.10s and 5.11s, with a smaller group of 5.12 and one 5.13 for the strong. Traditional gear is needed for a good share of the lines. The canyon is less busy than the main town walls, and its routes tend to dry out fairly quickly after rain, so it is a reasonable choice for a damp or hot day.
wa_toxic_tang_area.approach: Follow the Inner Walls trail up past the talus and over the small creek. Look left for the Toxic-Tang wall, which begins at the start of the notch and running west to a big hole called the cave, roughly 50 yards along.

wa_wart_the.blurb: A rounded rocky knoll about 100 feet tall sitting right beside the railroad tracks at the foot of the Lower Lump in Index, Washington. The granodiorite here holds around twenty routes, a fairly even split of sport and trad with a few set up for top-rope. Most of the climbing falls in the 5.9 and 5.10 range, with some easier routes in the 5.7 to 5.8 range and a couple of harder lines up to 5.13. The short approach is the same as for the rest of the Lower Lump, which is a quick walk from the parking pullouts, so it works well for a brief outing or a warm-up before heading to a steeper wall nearby.

wa_pretty_boulders.blurb: A bouldering zone along Icicle Creek Road, a short drive up the canyon from Leavenworth. It is a lightly visited alternative to the busier Mad Meadows and Forestland zones, with roughly two dozen problems that cover a very wide range: plenty of easy V0 to V1 lines, a solid middle of V3 to V5, and a few much harder problems reaching into the V8 to V10 range. Boulders are moderate in height rather than highball, and a pair of crash pads plus spotters are useful on the steeper ones. The walk from the road is short but fairly steep, and roadside space for cars is limited on busy weekends.
